Reference - Authors: Matthew N Mendoza; Mike Jian; Moeko T King; Cory L Brooks
Reference - Title: Role of a noncanonical disulfide bond in the stability, affinity, and flexibility of a VHH specific for the Listeria virulence factor InlB.
Epitope - Comments: The epitope residues were calculated from [PDB: 6U12] as the antigen residues at 4Å atomic distance from the antibody.
Immunization - Comments: Generation of the monoclonal antibody was previously described in the cited reference: Gene et al. (2015) J Immunol Methods 416:29-39 [PMID: 25450000]. Single-domain antibodies from the heavy chain antibody repertoire (VHH) of Camelidae, which bind with specificity and high affinity to the Listeria monocytogenes invasin, were isolated from a non-immune phage display library. To investigate if the noncanonical disulfide bond between CDR1 and CDR3 influences the affinity of the VHH R303 toward its antigen, a double cysteine to alanine mutation (C33A/C102A) was introduced by site directed mutagenesis to generate double mutant R303 (C33A/C102A).
Assay - Location of Assay Data in Refere: Figure 3, Table 1, Supplementary Table I and PDB 6U12
Assay - Comments: The epitope of R303 (C33A/C102A) on InlB 249 (aa 36-249) was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. The complex structure contained a single molecule of R303 (C33A/C102A) and InlB249.
